title: EV Charger Rebates in Sacramento 2026: Up to $850 from SMUD | HomePowerRebate
desc: SMUD's Charge@Home pays up to $100 for a charger, $200 for a circuit sharing device and $750 for the circuit, up to $850 on its page. Rules, specs and income-eligible help.
lead: SMUD's Charge@Home program pays up to $850 toward a home charger and its circuit. Most of the money is for the electrical work, not the charger, and income-eligible customers on SMUD's Energy Assistance Program Rate can get a charger and installation at no cost.
cards_intro: These figures come from SMUD's Charge@Home page and terms and conditions, which we read on October 2, 2026. Rebates are first come, first served and cannot exceed what you actually paid.

cards.title: EV charging unit
cards.note: For an eligible new charger: up to 32 amps on a 40-amp breaker, ENERGY STAR certified, with a 3-year warranty.

cards.title: Circuit sharing or energy management device
cards.note: For a device that lets the charger share a circuit and avoid a panel upgrade.

cards.title: Installing the circuit
cards.note: Through a contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network, with wire no larger than #8 copper.

cards.title: Income-eligible customers
cards.note: For customers on SMUD's Energy Assistance Program Rate (EAPR), through a separate application.

after_cards:
One rebate, once

SMUD's terms limit it to one combined rebate per account and address for life: one charger and device, and one installation. Plan the work so the charger and circuit are claimed together. SMUD's headline is up to $850 because the circuit ($750) and the charger ($100) are the usual pair. The $200 device is an alternative for homes that need to share a circuit.
sections: Your plug-in vehicle must be registered with the DMV at the same address as your SMUD residential account, and the name on the registration must match the name on the SMUD account. The program covers four-wheel light-duty passenger vehicles only, so motorcycles do not count. Payment is made in the name of the SMUD customer of record, by mail, 1 to 2 weeks after SMUD approves a complete application. If the vehicle is registered at a different address, fix that before you buy the charger.
The charger spec that rules out some models

SMUD wants a unit that supplies up to 32 amps (7.7 kW) on a circuit with a breaker of 40 amps or less, with a SAE J1772 or NACS connector, certified by a recognized test lab, ENERGY STAR certified, with a minimum 3-year warranty. A powerful 48-amp unit does not fit. SMUD publishes a list of eligible chargers, so check your model against it before you pay.

A full panel is the common problem. The $200 circuit sharing or energy management device lets a charger share a circuit and manage load, which can avoid a panel upgrade. If a larger change is needed, SMUD's Go Electric rebates pay up to $4,000 for a smart panel, subpanel or new circuit when a gas-to-electric conversion is part of the job (Sacramento heat pump rebates). SMUD also publishes an EV charging and electrical panel fact sheet.

SMUD pays more for the electrical work than Pasadena, whose charger rebate is $600 for an internet-connected unit (Pasadena), and its headline $850 is below LADWP's $1,500 (Los Angeles). SMUD's rates and programs for EV owners are on its residential electric vehicles pages, which we did not read in full.
The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. The federal credit for home charging equipment may have separate rules, so ask a tax professional.
claim_heading: How to claim the SMUD charger rebate
claim_steps: Check that the vehicle is registered at your SMUD service address, in the same name as the SMUD account.
Choose an eligible charger from SMUD's list: up to 32 amps, ENERGY STAR, with a 3-year warranty.
If you need a circuit, hire a contractor in the SMUD Contractor Network and pull the permit.
Choose Option A if you already bought the equipment, or Option B if an electrician will install it and process the rebate.
Send the signed application, the DMV registration, the receipts, and the contractor invoice and permit.
SMUD mails the payment 1 to 2 weeks after it approves a complete application.
faq: How much is the SMUD EV charger rebate?
Up to $850 on SMUD's page: up to $100 for a charger, up to $200 for a circuit sharing device and up to $750 for the circuit installation.
Can I claim it more than once?
No. SMUD allows one combined rebate per account and address for life.
It must be a four-wheel light-duty plug-in vehicle registered with the DMV at the SMUD service address, in the same name as the SMUD account.
Is there free help for low-income households?
Yes. Customers on SMUD's Energy Assistance Program Rate can get a free charger and installation through a separate application.
How long until I am paid?
SMUD says payment is mailed 1 to 2 weeks after it approves a complete application.
